data.outcome_summary: This OECD PISA 2022 Qatar factsheet summarizes how 15-year-old students in Qatar performed in mathematics, reading, and science, and how results changed over time (notably 2006–2022 and comparisons to 2018 and 2012). PISA 2022 used two two-hour subject tests with rotated booklets so that different students received different combinations of mathematics, reading, and science items, plus a background questionnaire for students and a questionnaire for school principals. The factsheet reports mean performance, proficiency-level attainment (e.g., Level 2 and Level 5/6), and uncertainty via 95% confidence intervals, and it highlights distributional changes such as narrowing gaps between top and bottom deciles in mathematics, reading, and science. It also reports subgroup patterns (socio-economic status, gender, immigrant background) and contextual indicators (belonging, discipline, safety, parental involvement, and COVID-related experiences), but it does not estimate any predictive ML model or provide model performance metrics. Methodological details on PV estimation and missing-data handling are not included in the factsheet text.
